children: Factory activity expanded in the U.S. in September for the ninth consecutive month, according to a survey of manufacturing firms.

The Institute for Supply Management's purchasing managers' index was 54.5 in September, compared with 54.6 in August. Readings above 50 indicate a sectoral expansion. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a reading of 54.9.
The new orders index expanded for the ninth consecutive month after four straight readings in contraction, registering 55.3, the survey said.
However, the prices index remained in expansion, registering 77.9, a notable increase of 6.8 percentage points compared with August's reading of 71.1.
The employment index reading of 52.7 is up 1.5 percentage points from August's figure of 51.2.
However, the supplier deliveries index indicated slowing performance for the 10th month in a row after one month in "faster" territory, the survey said.
In September, 40% of the comments were positive and 60% negative, with a 1-to-1.6 ratio of positive to negative sentiment, said Susan Spence, chair of the ISM.
